events.title: Ukraine: Meaning-Making Workshop Outcome Document: Cross-Cutting Demographic Realities for 2027 HNRP Planning
events.summary: Country: Ukraine Sources: CARE, NGO Girls, Protection Cluster, Ukraine Gender in Humanitarian Action Working Group, UN Women Please refer to the attached file. Single-layer vulnerability classifications obscure the dynamic, intersectional realities of the current crisis. Moving beyond status-based or geographic targeting to needs-based response requires anchoring interventions in actual socio-economic and demographic profiles derived from the latest assessments (MSNA, COD-PS, DTM, Rapid Gender Assessment, and specialized TWG consultations). This document presents the outcomes of the Meaning-Making Workshop 2026, consolidating gender, age, and disability considerations and translating them into actionable recommendations for the Humanitarian Needs and Response Plan (HNRP) 2027. The document was shared with and presented to the Inter-Cluster Coordination Group (ICCG), which brings together sector and cluster leads, in September 2026. It brings together the key materials and findings from the workshop, organized by the Gender in Humanitarian Action Working Group (GiHA WG) in collaboration with the Cross-Cutting Expertise Group—which includes the GiHA WG, Age and Disability Technical Working Group (TWG), Accountability to Affected People Working Group (AAP WG), and LGBTIQ+ Technical Working Group—as well as the Data Coordination Group, comprising REACH, IOM, and OCHA.

NEW YORK/JOHANNESBURG, NOVEMBER 26 — In advance of World AIDS Day on December 1, Doctors Without Borders/Médecins Sans Frontières (MSF) is once again calling for more people globally to have access to the highly effective HIV prevention medicine lenacapavir . This twice-yearly injectable version of pre-exposure prophylaxis (PrEP) is the biggest breakthrough in HIV prevention yet, but US-based Gilead Sciences continues to block affordable access for countries around the world. This includes countries with growing HIV epidemics and ongoing humanitarian crises. As a result of its long-acting nature, lenacapavir may be especially valuable for stigmatized or criminalized populations, who often are excluded from or concerned about accessing health care. It is also a critical tool for people on the move who may struggle to access health clinics, people living in remote areas with few health care options, and people caught in humanitarian emergencies — including those in many of the communities in which MSF operates. “Gilead’s greed alone is the reason people across the globe don’t have access to lenacapavir already,” said Carlota Baptista da Silva, MSF’s global HIV/HCV access and advocacy lead. “Our teams are ready to provide it but have been left empty-handed or with very few doses to offer. In a context emerging from years of largescale conflict, where some conditions have improved but localized violence, new and secondary displacement, and very high humanitarian needs persist in parts of the country, this allocation will fast-track lifesaving and life sustaining multisectoral assistance and protection for crisis affected people in 85 priority subdistricts, which record the highest intersectoral severity of needs and the highest prevalence of IDPs and returnees. The allocation will support the immediate kickstart of the hyper prioritized HNRP, targeting around 4.3 million women, men, girls, boys, older people and persons with disabilities with direct assistance in areas with the highest concentrations of IDPs, returnees and refugees. In this way, the Syria Humanitarian Fund will help translate the humanitarian reset roadmap into concrete action, using pooled funding to drive a principled, highly prioritized and locally empowered response: channeling resources to the most severe needs at speed and scale, minimizing layers and passthrough funding, enabling integrated and multisector programming by best placed actors, and strengthening collective accountability through transparent, evidence based allocation, enhanced monitoring and improved accountability to affected populations. Taken together, the fast‑track reserve, the CERF UFE allocation and the first SHF Standard Allocation form a single, sequenced funding package of over US$200 million designed to save lives in the first half of 2026, while structurally advancing localization through a target of around 75 per cent of SA1 resources to national NGOs and women‑led organizations.

En este escenario, la provisión de kits de enseres esenciales (EHIs) se convierte en un componente clave de la respuesta humanitaria, al garantizar que las personas puedan vivir adecuadamente y con dignidad en sus viviendas, facilitando la recuperación temprana y el retorno seguro a los hogares en las comunidades afectadas.

events.title: Somalia Humanitarian Fund (SHF) Quarterly Newsletter - Q2 & Q3 2026
events.summary: Country: Somalia Source: UN Office for the Coordination of Humanitarian Affairs Please refer to the attached file. SHF News Allocations In the second and third quarters of 2026, the Somalia Humanitarian Fund (SHF) undertook three critical allocations to address urgent humanitarian needs. In July 2026, the SHF allocated US$ 2 million to scale up response required to mitigate the risk of famine in rural areas of Buurhakaba, Bay Region. The allocation prioritized multisectoral lifesaving assistance to increase access to food, integrated health, nutrition, and protection (GBV) services; and improve access to water. The allocation was complemented by a $10 million CERF Rapid Response grant to sustain humanitarian assistance to mitigate the adverse effects of the prolonged drought conditions in additional areas. In anticipation of a forecast Super El Nino, CERF granted an additional $7 million to facilitate timely, targeted, multi-sectoral interventions in flood high-risk districts along the Juba and Shabelle river basins. Given the gravity of the humanitarian situation amid continuing funding shortfalls, SHF also launched a $21 million Standard Allocation in September to provide integrated multisectoral assistance across seven priority districts hosting underserved communities with the highest severity of needs, including heightened protection and flood risks. Some $13 million from this envelope targeted flood -prone locations. The collective allocation of $33 million from CERF and SHF enabled the strategic use of limited resources through geographic and sectoral convergence, and sectoral complementarity to deliver much needed assistance to vulnerable communities.

Fiji has one of the fastest-growing HIV epidemics globally, with new infections rising approximately twelvefold between 2010 and 2025 . events.summary: Country: Haiti Source: World Health Organization World Health Organization (WHO) Director-General, Dr Tedros Adhanom Ghebreyesus, today announced US$ 1 million in support for critical medical equipment in Haiti. Dr Tedros made the announcement during his visit to the country to reinforce WHO’s support for a health system under severe pressure from the ongoing humanitarian and security crisis. The funding will provide equipment to the overwhelmed Hôpital Universitaire La Paix (HUP) in the capital, Port-au-Prince, including a computed tomography (CT) scanner and equipment for four operating rooms. Armed violence in Haiti continues to severely disrupt access to health care, forcing numerous health facilities to close, displacing communities, and disrupting medical supply chains. The growing number of internally displaced persons (1.5 million to date) is placing additional pressure on an already overstretched health system.
